input.rationale: Both limbs of the assignment bargain sit at or beyond our walk-away line. Section (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149) imposes a one-way, blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment with no Affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while leaving Licensor free to assign (including to our competitors). Article XX(a) (p0134) then makes any Change of Control of Licensee — including a sale of substantially all assets or a merger (p0135) — an automatic termination of the Agreement and all of our licenses unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever the acquirer is competitive with it or it merely "believes" its interests are adversely affected. That is precisely the vendor change-of-control exit the playbook prohibits. Our redline makes the assignment right mutual with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, bars Licensor assignment to a Licensee competitor, applies a not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments, and converts Article XX(a) from a Licensor termination/consent trigger into a notice obligation while preserving the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition relied on elsewhere. Fallback if pressed: mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent not unreasonably withheld for other transfers.

proposal.summary: Add Affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Licensee, make consent standard mutual and reasonable, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a blanket bar on our assignment coupled with automatic termination of the licenses on our change of control, so we have made the assignment clause mutual with a carve-out for Affiliates and successors by merger or sale of substantially all assets, and a reasonableness standard on any other consent. We have also removed Licensor's change-of-control termination and consent right (Article XX(a)), replacing it with prompt written notice; if helpful, we can accept mutual assignment to successors with written notice as a fallback.

Any attempt to assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner Licensee's license rights hereunder without such consent will be void and of no effect. ops.newText: Either party may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the other party's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity, provided that Licensor may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Licensee. Except as permitted by the preceding sentence, neither party may assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its rights hereunder in whole or in part without the other party's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Any attempt to assign in violation of this Section will be void and of no effect. No Change of Control of Licensee shall be deemed an assignment for purposes of this Agreement or give Licensor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement

ops.oldText: (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control.
ops.newText: (a) A Change of Control (as defined below) of Licensee shall not require Licensor's consent and shall not terminate or suspend this Agreement or any of Licensee's rights or licenses hereunder, nor give Licensor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement; Licensee shall give Licensor written notice of such Change of Control promptly following its consummation.

ops.oldText: For purposes of the preceding sentence, Licensor will be deemed to have reasonably withheld its consent to a Change of Control if any person or entity who would acquire direct or indirect control (as defined below) of Licensee pursuant to such Change of Control then conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive with a business then conducted by Licensor or any of its Affiliates and/or Licensor reasonably believes that Licensor's interests will be adversely effected by the continuing of this Agreement upon such a Change in Control.
